fight: Enact/React foreground app vs vanilla JS service for HA companion — which survives sam/memoryd kills and offers keep-alive?

side_a.position: Enact requires foreground app for JS service lifecycle; vanilla JS service with ActivityManager keep-alive is more resilient
claims: JS service 5s idle timer kills inactive services; ActivityManager activity needed

side_b.position: Enact provides full UI for dashboard rendering; vanilla JS suffices only for headless
claims: Enact is LG-recommended for TV UI; JS service alone cannot render Lovelace

evidence_quality_delta: side_a stronger (official LG docs on idle timer)
scope_overlap: genuine disagreement — headless vs UI needs

fight: Homebrew Channel elevate-service vs com.webos.appInstallService/dev/install for rooted IPK install

side_a.position: Homebrew elevate-service (piccap pattern) is de-facto standard for rooted
claims: PicCap ships hyperion-webos via elevate-service; scp + luna-send dev/install works

side_b.position: Direct appInstallService is more portable and survives Homebrew removal

evidence_quality_delta: side_a stronger (live fingerprint on 10.1.1.209 uses Homebrew)

fight: Persistent WebSocket vs MQTT for HA local push between TV and coordinator

side_a.position: WebSocket re-uses bscpylgtv's ws:3000 channel and coordinator push model
claims: bscpylgtv already uses ws:3000 with subscriptions; WebSocket fits HA local_push

side_b.position: MQTT is HA-native for edge nodes and handles reconnect/retain better
claims: HA MQTT discovery auto-creates entities; broker handles last-will

scope_overlap: scoped differently — WS is peer-to-peer, MQTT needs broker

fight: WS SSAP 401 vs root luna-send privilege — is WS sufficient for new entities?

side_a.position: WS SSAP gated by appinfo requiredPermissions; many Luna endpoints return 401 without root
claims: probe on 10.1.1.209 returned 401 for getForegroundAppInfo over WS, but luna-send as root succeeded

side_b.position: Injecting requiredPermissions via appinfo can unlock some endpoints without root
claims: requiredPermissions in appinfo.json generates LS2 client permissions

fight: LG Content Store vs Homebrew Channel for distributing rooted companion IPK

side_a.position: Homebrew Channel is only viable for root-privileged perms; store would strip them
claims: requiredPermissions like all would be rejected by LG review

side_b.position: Store gives discoverability and auto-updates; some users prefer non-root
claims: Store apps can use devmode sideload for 50h sessions

evidence_quality_delta: side_a stronger for this use case
